stem: Find the number of forces in the F.B.D. of block 'A': a block m sits on a rough incline of angle θ, connected by a string over a pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block A of mass m.

Find the number of forces in the F.B.D. of block 'A': block m₁ rests on top of block m₂ (labelled A) which rests on the ground; the m₁–m₂ interface is rough and the m₂–ground interface is rough; a horizontal force F is applied to the upper block m₁.

stem: A 3 kg block on a rough horizontal table (μ s = 0.60, μ k = 0.45; wood on brick) is pulled by a force that ramps linearly from 0 to 30 N in 5 s. When does it start moving? (a) At 2.9 s; N = mg and F = μ s N decide the onset. (b) Never; μ s increases with time. (c) At 1.5 s; sliding starts earlier than limiting friction. (d) At 5.0 s by definition of the ramp end.

A horizontal force of 10 N is necessary to hold a block stationary against a vertical wall. The coefficient of friction between the block and the wall is 0.2. The weight of the block is: (a) 20 N (b) 50 N (c) 100 N (d) 2 N.

A block of mass 0.1 kg is held against a wall by applying a horizontal force of 5 N on the block. If the coefficient of friction between the block and the wall is 0.5, the magnitude of the friction force acting on the block is: (a) 2.5 N (b) 0.98 N (c) 4.9 N (d) 0.49 N.

A block is pulled to the right at constant velocity by a force of 10 N acting 30° above the horizontal. If the coefficient of sliding friction between the block and the surface is 0.5, the weight of the block is: (a) 20 N (b) 22.32 N (c) 56 N (d) 72.4 N.
